canonical_statement: The study evaluated the association between SSRI/SNRI use and new-onset long-COVID manifestations in children and adolescents with documented neuropsychiatric conditions.
This was a retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data from 37 US children’s hospitals and healthcare systems participating in the NIH RECOVER Initiative.
Eligible participants were older than 5 years and younger than 21 years at cohort entry.

population.label: Eligible pediatric age range
inclusion_criteria: Older than 5 years and younger than 21 years at cohort entry

canonical_statement: Eligible participants required a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection during cohort entry from 1 March 2020 through 22 September 2023 and a pre-existing neuropsychiatric condition.

population.label: Infection and neuropsychiatric eligibility
inclusion_criteria: Documented SARS-CoV-2 infection during cohort entry period

canonical_statement: Participants were required to have at least one healthcare encounter during the baseline period 24 months to 7 days before infection and at least one encounter during follow-up 28–179 days after infection.

population.label: Encounter requirements
inclusion_criteria: At least one healthcare encounter 24 months to 7 days before infection
At least one healthcare encounter 28–179 days after infection

canonical_statement: The final analytic cohort contained 110,955 participants, including 12,416 SSRI/SNRI users and 98,539 nonusers.

canonical_statement: Of the 110,955 participants, 12,416 (11.2%) were classified as SSRI/SNRI users and 98,539 (88.8%) as nonusers.

population.label: Children and adolescents aged 5–20 years with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection and pre-existing neuropsychiatric conditions

canonical_statement: SSRI/SNRI users were participants receiving an included SSRI or SNRI during the window from 28 days before through 28 days after the index SARS-CoV-2 infection date.

exposures.details: Exposure window: 28 days before to 28 days after index infection

canonical_statement: Included SSRIs were citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine and sertraline; included SNRIs were desvenlafaxine, duloxetine and venlafaxine.

exposures.details: Citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, or sertraline

canonical_statement: Participants not meeting the SSRI/SNRI exposure definition were classified as non-SSRI/SNRI.

exposures.details: Did not receive an included SSRI/SNRI in the exposure window

canonical_statement: Among exposed participants, 90.7% received SSRIs and 9.3% received SNRIs.

population.label: SSRI/SNRI-exposed participants

canonical_statement: One long-COVID definition was a clinician-recorded ICD-10-CM U09.9 diagnosis during follow-up.

outcome.definition: Assessed 28–179 days after index infection among patients without prior documentation of the condition

canonical_statement: A complementary long-COVID definition comprised 23 prespecified symptoms or clinical conditions potentially linked to pediatric long COVID.

concept.text: Any occurrence of 23 prespecified long-COVID symptoms/conditions

outcome.definition: Assessed 28–179 days after index infection; outcome-specific analyses excluded patients with the same condition documented at baseline

canonical_statement: Outcome incidence was calculated as the proportion of at-risk participants without the condition at baseline who developed the outcome during the fixed 28–179-day follow-up window.
Confounding was addressed with propensity score stratification using pre-index covariates; post-stratification standardized mean difference of 0.1 or less was considered acceptable balance.
Adjusted relative risks and 95% confidence intervals were estimated with modified Poisson regression models.
Prespecified subgroup analyses examined age, sex, race/ethnicity, obesity status and acute COVID-19 severity.
Sensitivity analyses excluded selected neuropsychiatric diagnoses and pre-U09.9-era infections, and 26 negative-control outcomes were used to assess residual bias.
Female participants comprised 68.7% of SSRI/SNRI users and 50.6% of nonusers.

canonical_statement: The authors reported that findings were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses in Supplementary Tables 5–18.
None of the 26 negative-control outcomes showed a significant association with SSRI/SNRI exposure.
The authors concluded that SSRI/SNRI use was not associated with clinician-recorded long-COVID diagnosis but showed heterogeneous associations with individual post-COVID symptoms and conditions.
The authors stated that the findings warrant further investigation and support personalized risk assessment and monitoring rather than a simple protective or harmful interpretation of SSRI/SNRI use.
The retrospective design and reliance on EHR data may cause misclassification of SARS-CoV-2 infection status or outcomes.
Residual confounding may remain despite statistical adjustment, including from unmeasured socioeconomic status or family psychiatric history.
Differences in healthcare utilization between exposure groups may influence symptom and diagnosis documentation.
The study did not perform chart validation, and evolving definitions of long COVID may reduce interpretability.
The observed SSRI/SNRI exposure prevalence of 11.2% exceeded cited national pediatric antidepressant-use estimates and may limit generalizability.
For fluctuating conditions, EHR data may not reliably distinguish recurrence of a pre-existing problem from a truly incident post-COVID manifestation.

The Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary described the study as a quantitative observational study using non-random convenience sampling of eligible pediatric EHR patients; experimental blinding was not applicable.
The research was funded by NIH Agreement OTA OT2HL161847-01 as part of the RECOVER Initiative.
L. Charles Bailey reported grants from the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; the other authors declared no competing interests.
Individual-level RECOVER patient data are not publicly released because of re-identification risk; access requests are directed to the RECOVER EHR Pediatric Coordinating Center.
The analysis code is reported as available through Code Ocean at DOI 10.24433/CO.4519602.v1.
